newsitem.title: INDIA: Yamaha plans world's top motorbike unit in India.
newsitem.headline: Yamaha plans world's top motorbike unit in India.

text.p: Japan's Yamaha Motor Company said on Thursday that it planned to set up the world's biggest motorcycle factory in India through a joint venture with India's Escorts Ltd.

Yamaha's president, Takehiko Yasegawa, and Escorts Ltd's vice-chairman, Anil Nanda, told a news conference in the Indian capital that the venture, currently a collaboration focusing on India, would grow to seek global markets.
"We have come to the agreement that we will establish the biggest motorcycle factory in the world sometime not very far from today in the early part of the 21st century," Yasegawa said.

The joint venture would start making scooters in a new $42 million plant and invest 3.75 billion rupees ($105 million) in upgrading two motorcycle plants sold off by Escorts Ltd to the joint venture, Escorts Yamaha Motor Ltd, company officials said.

Escorts Yamaha plans to introduce four new models of motorcycles over the next two years, and in 1999 make a cautious entry into India's huge scooter market by making the nation's first four-stroke engine model, they said.
The venture, in which Escorts and Yamaha currently hold 50 percent each, would expand its total equity to 520 million rupees ($14.6) from 100 million $2.8 million), they said.
The firm would offer 48 percent of its total equity to the public in the middle of 1997, after which Escorts and Yamaha would hold 26 percent each in the joint venture.
Escorts Yamaha made 189,000 motorcycles in 1995/96 (April-March), holding a 28 percent market share in the Indian market.
Output was expected to grow to 252,000 in 1996/97, and the market share to 33 percent, company officials said.
Yasegawa said output of motorcycles was expected to grow to 550,000 in 2000 and to 700,000 in 2005.
Sales are expected to grow to 9.0 billion rupees in 1996/97 and 20 billion ($56 million) in 2000 from around 6.0 billion rupees ($169 million) in 1995/96.

The joint venture has bought two motorcycle plants earlier owned by Escorts Ltd, which has been one of India's leading motorcycle makers. Much of the fresh investment would be to upgrade the two plants, company officials said.
